fichas.title: Hospital Supply Area
fichas.summary: Commercial and technical supplies enter through a separate service building or a neutral basement supply and waste-disposal level. Delivery access should be separated from the main entrance and stretcher arrivals; locating delivery and waste areas to the north is described as ideal. Routes should limit interaction with care and treatment traffic. The area may cause noise and odour nuisance, and supply and waste services are increasingly centralised or outsourced.

fichas.title: Sterile Goods Supply
fichas.summary: The central sterile store should be near the surgical department and is organised by the flow of materials through acceptance, pre-cleaning, washing, sterilisation, packing and sterile storage. It prepares instruments for hospital use. The text identifies surgery and intensive-care departments as major users and notes that the number of sterilisers depends on hospital and surgical-department size.

HOSPITALS
Supply and Waste Disposal

Supply area
Commercial and technical supply enters the hospital either via
a separate service building or at a neutral supply and waste
disposal level (basement) under the main building. There should
be an access for deliveries into the service yard, separated from
the main entrance and the arrival of patients on stretchers. The
location of delivery and waste disposal areas to the north is
ideal. External and internal traffic routes should be designed so
that interaction with the traffic in the care and treatment areas is
avoided as much as possible.

0 Supply centre, Cologne University Clinic: kitchen, prepared stores
Arch.: Heinie, Wischer und Partner Freie Architekten

kitchen,

Sterile goods supply
The central sterile store should be near the surgical department,
the largest consumer (smaller stores of sterile goods in the theatres themselves are no longer needed). The layout is structured
according to the direction of flow of materials into acceptance,
pre-cleaning, washing machine, sterilisers, packing zone and
sterile goods store. All the instruments for use in the hospital are
prepared here. The departments with particularly heavy use are
surgery with 40% and operative intensive care and internal intensive care with 15% each.

hospital can potentially cause noise and odour nuisance (waste
containers, kitchen waste, etc.). There is a noticeable tendency
towards increasing centralisation of supply and waste disposal
facilities and also the outsourcing of certain functional areas (e.g.
laundry, kitchen).

Dispensary: In hospitals without a full pharmacy, medicines
requiring approval are issued from the dispensary. This consists
of work and dispensing rooms with direct access to the circulation
corridor. The equipment consists of desk, washbasin, sink,

a dressings room and a darnp store according to fire regulations.
Bed preparation

even in the room.

Pharmaceutical supply
Pharmacy: In medium-sized and large hospitals, the pharmacy
stores formulations and carries out the production of drugs under
the management of a qualified pharmacist. For design purposes,
the rooms required are dispensary, materials room, drug store,
laboratory and possibly also issue desk. Rooms may also be
required for herbs, dressings, substance storage, on-call room.
The equipment of pharmacy and laboratory includes formulation
table, work or packing table and a sink. The fitting out is similar
to that of the dispensary. The location of the pharmacy should
involve a short route to the lifts, pneumatic post etc. Since firehazardous substances and acids are stored here as well as
various narcotics, the walls, ceilings and doors need to meet
security standards.

Arch.: U. +A. Weicken

Pushing numbers of beds through the building and the heavy
mechanical wear and wetting of the beds, usual in central bed
processing, is no longer necessary. It can, however, be sensible to
provide for separate disinfection of mattresses in the basement,
possibly combined with a bed repair roorn.

fichas.title: Pharmaceutical Supply: Pharmacy and Dispensary
fichas.summary: Medium-sized and large hospitals may have a pharmacy that stores formulations and produces drugs under a qualified pharmacist. Required spaces may include a dispensary, materials room, drug store, laboratory and issue desk, with additional stores or rooms as needed. The pharmacy should have a short route to lifts and pneumatic post; fire-hazardous substances, acids and narcotics require secure construction. Hospitals without a full pharmacy may issue medicines requiring approval through a dispensary, with work and dispensing rooms directly accessible from the circulation corridor and adjacent medicine stores.

fichas.title: Bed Preparation
fichas.summary: Used beds and mattresses are normally disinfected by spray-and-wipe methods in the ward or room. Central bed processing that moves large numbers of beds through the building, with associated mechanical wear and wetting, is described as no longer necessary. Separate mattress disinfection in the basement may be provided, possibly combined with a bed repair room.
